raw_response.country: Multi-country / global (55 countries and 47 other constituencies across sub-Saharan Africa, Middle East and North Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean, East Asia and Pacific, South Asia, Europe, North America, and global institutions; individual country names not reported)

criterion_notes.c1: No. Although situated in the WASH sector and SDG 6 policy context, the study does not examine household or community water or sanitation service access; its unit of analysis is the text of 291 voluntary policy commitment statements submitted to the global Sanitation and Water for All (SWA) partnership database.
criterion_notes.c2: Plain wording vs. narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading: Under the plain broad wording of Criterion 2 ('legal, administrative, institutional, regulatory or governance factor'), the paper would satisfy Criterion 2 because it examines a multi-stakeholder WASH governance mechanism (SWA's Mutual Accountability Mechanism) and classifies national/stakeholder commitments across governance building blocks, functions, and attributes. However, under the active 2026-10-13 clarification, Criterion 2 is 'no': high-level voluntary partnership goal-setting, SMART target drafting, and broad macro-governance categories (e.g., sector policy/strategy, planning, coordination) are not rule-type mechanisms directly governing service access (such as eligibility screening, administrative burden, documentation/tenure rules, tariffs, discretion, enforcement, or utility regulatory/ownership structures). Note that even under the plain reading of Criterion 2, the overall decision remains 'exclude' because no WASH service access outcomes are measured (c1=no, c4=no).
criterion_notes.c3: Yes. The authors conduct an empirical deductive content analysis and univariate descriptive frequency analysis of 291 commitment entries recorded in the SWA MAM Airtable database between 1 March 2019 and 21 January 2020.
criterion_notes.c4: No. The reported outcomes are solely textual characteristics of voluntary commitment statements—specifically, relative tag frequencies of governance components (e.g., sector policy/strategy, efficiency, enabling conditions) and Specific, Measurable, and Time-bound (SMT) goal-writing criteria. The authors explicitly state that their analysis is limited to the commitment texts in the database and does not assess implementation processes or concrete impacts on WASH access, reliability, or affordability.
criterion_notes.c5: No. While the content-analysis design and sample of 291 commitment entries are identifiable, there is no household or community service-user population, no rule-type mechanism governing service access as exposure, and no real-world WASH access outcome.
criterion_notes.c6: Yes. Full text is written in English.

evidence_quotes.quote: The aim of this paper is to analyse the SWA commitments in relation to water governance frameworks in order to provide speciﬁc recommendations for the improvement of target composition.
This research includes all commitments made between March 2019, shortly after the MAM was launched, and January 2020, representing 291 commitments by 55 countries and 47 other constituencies.
Secondly, we applied a deductive content analysis to focus on conceptualizing and describing the commitments included in the SWA MAM database.
This analysis focuses only on the commitments in the SWA database and does not take into account the MAM process or impact. The data are therefore limited to the commitments in the database.

The analysis of building blocks and governance functions revealed that commitments were tagged with comparatively high frequency as sector policy/strategy (56.7%) or planning, monitoring and review (25.4%)

raw_response.exposure: Stakeholder constituency type (government, civil society, external support agencies, research and learning, private sector) and SWA Mutual Accountability Mechanism (MAM) voluntary commitment framework
raw_response.outcome: Textual tag frequencies of water governance components (building blocks, functions, attributes, intended outcomes) and Specific, Measurable, and Time-bound (SMT) goal formulation attributes in voluntary commitment statements
raw_response.population_and_sample: 291 voluntary WASH commitment statements submitted between 1 March 2019 and 21 January 2020 by 55 countries and 47 other stakeholder constituencies in the Sanitation and Water for All (SWA) Mutual Accountability Mechanism online database
raw_response.rationale: Excluded (E04: Wrong outcome; also fails c1 and narrow c2). This empirical content analysis audits the text of 291 voluntary WASH commitments in the Sanitation and Water for All (SWA) Mutual Accountability Mechanism database for governance-theme tags and SMART goal-setting attributes. It explicitly does not examine implementation or measure any real-world household or community WASH access, connection, reliability, continuity, or affordability outcomes, nor does it evaluate a rule-type legal or administrative mechanism directly governing service access. Even under the plain broad wording of Criterion 2, the study remains excluded because it reports no service access outcomes.
raw_response.study_design: Deductive content analysis and descriptive univariate frequency analysis of voluntary partnership commitment statements
